博多ラーメン.summary: Fukuoka's ramen pairs a rich, milky broth made by slowly simmering pork bones with very thin, straight noodles. The noodles are thin so they do not go soft, and you can choose their firmness when ordering, from barikata (very firm) to futsu (regular). There is a culture of kaedama, ordering just a refill of noodles, so locals save some broth for a second helping. Change the flavor with pickled ginger, spicy mustard greens or sesame on the table. Try it at the yatai food stalls in Nakasu for the full experience.

博多もつ鍋.summary: Hakata's famous hot pot of tender beef offal, such as small intestine, simmered with plenty of cabbage, garlic chives and garlic. Soy sauce and miso broths are the most common, combining the rich umami of the offal with the sweetness of the vegetables. It was born in Hakata and has even sparked a nationwide craze. Finish by adding champon noodles to the leftover soup, or make rice porridge. Most restaurants serve it for two or more people, so it is best enjoyed in a group. It warms you up on a cold day.
